claims.text: Surface lattice distortions induced by compositional heterogeneity drive the onset and progression of the phase transition in FeNiCrCoCu nanoparticles.
Surface lattice distortions locally reduce the melting point at the exterior of FeNiCrCoCu nanoparticles.
The starting FeNiCrCoCu nanoparticles have a homogeneous elemental distribution.
Compositional randomness produces local lattice distortions at nanoparticle surfaces.
Surface-induced lattice distortions are more pronounced in particles with higher surface-to-volume ratios.
The random distribution of elements having different atomic radii causes significant lattice distortion in FeNiCrCoCu.
Lattice distortion is especially strong at the particle surface.
Surface lattice distortions reduce local cohesive energy.
Reduced local cohesive energy lowers the effective surface melting temperature.
Premelting begins at the surface and expands progressively inward as temperature increases.
Particles with greater surface exposure will exhibit an earlier onset of premelting than particles with mitigated surface effects.
Unpassivated particles will exhibit an earlier onset of premelting than passivated particles.
Loss of crystalline order will progress from the particle surface toward its interior.
The proposed surface-dominated behavior applies under inert or vacuum conditions with minimal oxidation.
The thermal response may differ in bulk samples or oxidizing environments.
A passivating layer can suppress surface atomic rearrangements while leaving particle composition and size distribution otherwise comparable.
Indistinguishable premelting onset temperatures and melting-progression profiles for passivated and unpassivated particles would falsify the proposed surface-distortion mechanism.

contradictions.description: The predicted-outcome field treats unpassivated or untreated particles as the high-surface-effect group expected to premelt earlier, but it also includes untreated particles in the stated comparison baseline. The actual baseline is therefore ambiguous between a room-temperature initial state and a thermal comparator group.
